subject: Liability cap approach for BrightScale order form
messages:
From: BrightScale Inc. <procurement@brightscale.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ellen.cho@brightscale-legal.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order form liability cap — initial ask

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightScale is excited about the integration. Procurement asked me to reach out specifically on the liability cap language for the order form / MSA. Our legal team is sensitive to large one-time exposures; we typically push for an annualized cap (fees paid in the prior 12 months) or a multiple of monthly recurring fees to ensure liability scales with consumption.

Two quick asks: can you share Redwood's standard position on overall cap (total contract vs rolling 12 months) and any standard multipliers you normally accept? Also, if you have a redline of the order form we can review that would be helpful.

We expect to circulate a draft redline from our counsel after an initial proposal.

Attaching: BrightScale-MSA_Request_20261101.pdf (procurement summary)

Best,
Amit Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightScale Inc.
[Attachment: BrightScale-MSA_Request_20261101.pdf (PDF, 28KB)]

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-01T11:00:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Order form liability cap — initial ask

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding BrightScale's procurement note. They explicitly prefer an annualized approach (fees paid in prior 12 months) or a multiple of monthly fees.

Notes / asks from sales side:
- BrightScale is mid-market but forecasted to grow quickly (expected 2–3x ARR year-over-year). Procurement wants an exposure that scales annually rather than a single contract-term cap.
- They will likely push for: 12x trailing monthly fees (i.e., annualized), or a cap equal to fees paid in prior 12 months.
- We should decide whether to offer: (A) rolling 12-month fees (common Redwood ask), or (B) total contract lifetime cap expressed as multiple of projected fees (riskier for us if they spike).

Proposed counter (sales preference): start with Redwood standard = "cap equals fees paid in the preceding 12 months" (simple and widely accepted). If procurement presses for lower cap, consider offering a multiple-of-fees option as alternative: "cap = greater of fees paid in preceding 12 months or 3x average monthly fees" — but need legal sign-off on multiplier and carveouts.

Also: keep standard exclusions (IP indemnity, fraud, gross negligence, wilful misconduct) and preserve exclusion for consequential damages but leave mediator for data breach carve-out if they insist.

Do you have a recommended multiplier range? Any guidance on annual-reset vs aggregate total? I can share a redline if you want to present a concrete starting point.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Internal note: prioritizing a clean, simple annualized cap minimizes procurement friction while limiting our downside on unexpected term spikes.]

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: BrightScale Inc. <procurement@brightscale.com>, Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@brightscale-legal.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-01T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Order form liability cap — proposed starting point

Hi Amit / Ellen,

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick starting proposal from Redwood to keep the negotiation moving:

1) Liability cap (general) — Redwood proposes a cap on direct damages equal to the fees paid by BrightScale to Redwood in the 12 months preceding the claim. This is a rolling 12-month lookback (annualized) rather than an aggregate lifetime cap. Rationale: aligns exposure with current usage and is standard for SaaS customers with variable consumption.

2) Multiple-of-fees option — if BrightScale needs an explicit multiplier, Redwood could offer a negotiated alternative: cap equal to the greater of (i) fees paid in the preceding 12 months, or (ii) 2x the annualized fees (i.e., ~24 months equivalent). We prefer to avoid >3x multipliers for growth-stage customers due to runaway exposure risk.

3) Carve-outs — Redwood proposes the following carve-outs to the cap (these remain uncapped): IP infringement indemnity; claims for willful misconduct or gross negligence; claims arising from Redwood's intentional breach of data security obligations (narrowly tailored); third-party claims where Redwood has indemnity obligations. Consequential/indirect damages will be excluded as standard, except to the extent of any indemnified claims.

4) Mitigation / SLO credits — we can keep a remedies ladder (credits tied to SLO breaches) and explicit mitigation obligations that factor into damages calculation.

Attached: Redwood-Proposed-OrderForm_Redline_20261101.pdf (highlights the cap language and carveouts)

If this is acceptable as a starting point I suggest Ellen and your counsel send a redline back with the specific numbers they prefer (e.g., 1x vs 2x vs 3x) and any carveout expansions. We are open to a defined annual-reset mechanism (rolling 12-month) so long as IP and security indemnities remain uncapped.

Next step: happy to hop on a short call this week to walk through the redline.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123
[Attachment: Redwood-Proposed-OrderForm_Redline_20261101.pdf (PDF, 52KB)]

From: Ellen Cho <ellen.cho@brightscale-legal.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Amit Patel <procurement@brightscale.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Order form liability cap — BrightScale redline

Laura / team,

Thanks for the proposal and the redline. BrightScale's counsel reviewed and attached a marked-up set of edits (see attached). High-level summary of our counterpoints:

- Annualized cap preferred: we remain firm that a rolling 12-month fees lookback is preferable to a single contract-wide cap. It limits exposure in any given year while ensuring long-term recoverability.
- Multiplier: BrightScale is willing to accept 1x trailing 12 months as a floor, but asks Redwood accept up to 3x annualized fees if certain data-processing exposures exist (i.e., where BrightScale is materially impacted by data loss or leakage that fits within our indemnity carveouts). The 3x ask is conditional and we included language to trigger a higher cap only where Redwood materially breaches security obligations.

- Carve-outs & consequential damages: we agree on preserving consequential damages exclusion but pushed to limit the "security breach" carveout narrowly so that only willful or grossly negligent conduct by Redwood will be uncapped. We also asked for specific carveouts around third-party processing subcontractors.

- Calculation mechanics: BrightScale requested clearer formulas for "fees paid in the preceding 12 months" (e.g., whether credits, discounts, and refunded charges are excluded). We proposed that fees be net of credits and refunds and measured on a trailing 12-month invoiced basis.

Attached: BrightScale-Counsel-Redline_20261103.pdf (PDF, 64KB) — includes suggested redline text for a conditional multiplier and a clarified fee-definition section.

We'll plan to be flexible on multiplier but need explicit triggers and a clear definition for fees calculation. Happy to join a call mid-next week with legal + sales to resolve the mechanics.

Best,
Ellen Cho
Senior Counsel, BrightScale Legal
ellen.cho@brightscale-legal.com
[Attachment: BrightScale-Counsel-Redline_20261103.pdf (PDF, 64KB)]
